newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast prods weaken on flush supply, NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast prods weaken on flush supply, NYMEX.

text.p: Most U.S. West Coast product prices eroded late Friday, as flush supplies and a weaker NYMEX pushed values back into their two-week slide, traders said.

Gasoline supplies, which stand 3.4 million barrels over stocks at this time last year, prompted traders to roll November positions into December barrels this week, leaving the market top-heavy with sellers.
December heating oil fell 0.79 cents a gallon to 72.61 cents a gallon, while unleaded gasoline dropped 200 points, as U.S. Gulf Coast cash prices weakened under heavy selling.
Los Angeles conventional gasoline fell 0.50 cents a gallon to 58.50/59.50 from early levels, with perceptions of too much gasoline on hand at refineries.
Bids for CARB-grade in Los Angeles fell a 0.25 cent to 62 while offers dropped a half cent to 62.75 cents a gallon.

San Francisco CARB gasoline saw its discount to L.A. widen from three cents to four, traders said, on perceptions that northern markets had more supply relative to L.A.. Southern supplies were dogged by concerns about refinery upsets.
Traders said Chevron would extend maintenance work on its El Segundo, Calif., refinery, and Texaco had to borrow supplies earlier this week after a hydrotreater burned, dealers said.
Los Angeles Jet fuel bucked the downtrend, rising a notional 2.50 cents a gallon to 71 cents Friday, on rumors of cargoes leaving for Asia.
